input.strategy_title: Default Vector Store for Gen AI Studio and Auto Rag
input.strategy_markdown:
## Summary

RHOAI must provide a default vector store that is available out-of-the-box — without manual setup — so that Gen AI Studio and Auto Rag continue to function when inline providers are removed from the Llama Stack distribution image. Today these capabilities depend on an inline vector store provider bundled within the Llama Stack process; removing it (per RHAISTRAT-7474) will break them unless an alternative is available at the platform level.

## Problem Statement

Gen AI Studio and Auto Rag currently rely on an inline Milvus provider embedded in the Llama Stack distribution image to store and retrieve vector embeddings. This inline provider runs inside the Llama Stack process itself.

RHAISTRAT-7474 proposes removing inline providers from the Llama Stack distribution to improve GA readiness — shipping only what can be tested and maintained at scale, and aligning with Llama Stack's primary use case as a remote API server. However, no platform-level alternative exists today. If inline providers are removed without a replacement, any RHOAI user relying on Gen AI Studio's RAG capabilities or Auto Rag will lose functionality entirely — there is no workaround short of manually provisioning and configuring an external vector database.

Users expect vector storage to "just work" when they use Gen AI Studio or Auto Rag. The current out-of-the-box experience must be preserved even as the underlying architecture evolves.

## Affected Customers

* All RHOAI customers using Gen AI Studio playground with RAG capabilities
* All RHOAI customers using Auto Rag
* This is a platform-level product dependency: these features cannot function without a vector store

## Business Justification

* **Product integrity:** Gen AI Studio and Auto Rag are GA-track capabilities in RHOAI. Removing the inline vector store without a replacement breaks shipped product functionality for every user of these features.
* **Blocking dependency:** RHAISTRAT-7474 (removing inline providers for GA readiness) cannot proceed until this RFE is resolved. Silas Brenmark (Gen AI Studio lead) has identified this as a blocker.
* **User experience:** RHOAI differentiates on integrated, opinionated defaults. Requiring users to manually provision and configure a vector database before they can use the playground or Auto Rag degrades the out-of-the-box experience that customers expect from the platform.

## Acceptance Criteria

* \[ \] A default vector store is available out-of-the-box on RHOAI without requiring users to manually provision or configure external infrastructure
* \[ \] Gen AI Studio playground RAG workflows function with the default vector store with no loss of current capability
* \[ \] Auto Rag functions with the default vector store with no loss of current capability
* \[ \] The default vector store runs as a separate process, decoupled from the Llama Stack instance (not an inline provider)
* \[ \] The default vector store is scoped appropriately for multi-tenant environments (e.g., per-namespace isolation)
* \[ \] The default vector store is lightweight enough to run in resource-constrained environments without imposing significant overhead

## Success Criteria

* Users of Gen AI Studio and Auto Rag experience no functional regression when inline providers are removed from the Llama Stack distribution
* No additional manual setup steps are required for RAG workflows compared to the current experience
* RHAISTRAT-7474 is unblocked and can proceed to implementation

## Open Questions

* What is the preferred scoping model — per namespace, per Llama Stack instance, or both? (Silas noted per-namespace is preferred for isolation, but Auto Rag may need per-instance scoping)
* Should users have a migration path from the default vector store to a production-grade vector database? (Bram Sundqvist raised the importance of aligning with commonly-used vector DB providers for easier migration)

## Strategy (AI Generated by Agentic SDLC Pipeline)

> **Note:** The full strategy exceeds Jira's description size limit and is stored as an attachment: `RHAISTRAT-8004-strategy.md`.

## Staff Engineer Input

**Correction 1 — OGX does not auto-provision PostgreSQL.** OGX defaults to SQLite for storage (`storage.kv.type: sqlite`, `storage.sql.type: sqlite` in the OGXServer CRD). The odh-dashboard gen-ai BFF hardcodes SQLite when creating OGXServer instances for the playground (`kv_sqlite` and `sql_sqlite` in `llamastack_config.go`). PostgreSQL is a supported backend but must be user-configured with an explicit `connectionString` secret. The strategy's claim that "every LlamaStackDistribution instance requires a PostgreSQL database" is incorrect — introducing PostgreSQL is new work, not an extension of existing infrastructure.

**Correction 2 — A Red Hat PostgreSQL image with pgvector already exists.** The `registry.redhat.io/rhel9/postgresql-16` image includes pgvector out of the box — confirmed in the [sclorg/postgresql-container Dockerfile](https://github.com/sclorg/postgresql-container/blob/master/16/Dockerfile.rhel9) (`INSTALL_PKGS="$INSTALL_PKGS pgvector"`). PostgreSQL 18 (RHEL 9) also includes pgvector. Furthermore, the model-registry-operator already uses `postgresql-16` as its auto-provisioned database image, and `RELATED_IMAGE_POSTGRESQL_16_IMAGE` is already present in the rhods-operator CSV for disconnected installs. No custom image build is needed. No Konflux onboarding is needed. The 1-2 sprint image onboarding estimate in the strategy can be eliminated.

**Architectural direction — platform-level database vs. self-provisioned.** Multiple RHOAI components now need PostgreSQL (model-registry, MLflow, and now OGX for pgvector). The preferred long-term direction is a platform-provided shared PostgreSQL managed via the DSC, where each component consumes a connection string rather than self-provisioning. A shared platform-provided PostgreSQL via DSC will not be available until RHOAI 3.6. For 3.5, Gen AI Studio must provision its own PostgreSQL instance.

**Operator dependency for self-provisioning (RHAISTRAT-7164).** Self-provisioning PostgreSQL following the model-registry-operator pattern requires a RHOAI-controlled operator for Gen AI Studio. The ogx-k8s-operator is upstream and cannot carry RHOAI-specific provisioning logic. The dashboard operator modularization (RHAISTRAT-7164, In Progress) would provide this operator layer. This is a hard dependency — until RHAISTRAT-7164 delivers, there is no RHOAI-controlled operator where PostgreSQL lifecycle management can live. It will be challenging to commit this strategy to a specific release until that dependency is delivered.

**Fallback if RHAISTRAT-7164 does not land in time.** If the dashboard modularization is not ready for 3.5, the fallback is to require customers to bring their own PostgreSQL for RAG capabilities in the Playground. Users would manually configure the OGXServer CR spec with their PostgreSQL connection details. This aligns with the breaking changes introduced in OGX 1.0, even though the Playground largely abstracts OGX from users. The development team should define a go/no-go gate for this decision as part of sprint planning.

**Decouple from Auto Rag.** Auto Rag integration with Gen AI Studio (RHAISTRAT-7824) is targeting RHOAI 3.6. This strategy should validate pgvector only for Gen AI Studio Playground RAG workflows. Auto Rag compatibility with pgvector will be addressed in RHAISTRAT-7824's scope. Remove Auto Rag from affected components, impacted teams, acceptance criteria, and validation requirements.

**Performance and index thresholds — dev experimentation scope.** The default pgvector instance is meant for development experimentation, not production usage. Strict latency SLAs (p50/p95/p99) are not required. The sprint 1 benchmark should capture the inline Milvus baseline and verify pgvector is in the same order of magnitude, not meet a specific threshold. Typical Playground RAG usage involves small document sets — flat scan (no index) is sufficient for the default. Users with production-scale vector workloads should use an external vector database. Remove open questions about latency thresholds, corpus size ranges, and index type selection.

**PostgreSQL resource sizing.** Reference the model-registry-operator's PostgreSQL resource requests/limits as the starting point. Adjust based on sprint 1 benchmarking if needed.

**Alternative fallback — BFF-managed PostgreSQL provisioning.** If RHAISTRAT-7164 does not land in time, an alternative to requiring customers to bring their own PostgreSQL is to have the gen-ai BFF provision the PostgreSQL/pgvector instance directly, similar to how the BFF currently provisions guardrails infrastructure. The BFF would create the PostgreSQL Deployment, Service, PVC, and Secret when a playground with RAG is configured, if one does not already exist in the namespace. Caveats: (1) the implementation must be designed for portability — when the platform-provided shared database becomes available (3.6), the BFF should consume the shared connection string rather than self-provisioning; (2) lifecycle management of the PostgreSQL instance must be carefully considered — the BFF is not an operator with a reconciliation loop, so cleanup on playground deletion, handling of pod restarts, and credential rotation need explicit design attention.

**Existing remote vector store implementation is reusable.** Per the engineering team, the existing remote vector store implementation can be largely reused for pgvector integration. The majority of the work effort is around infrastructure and provisioning of the PostgreSQL/pgvector database, not the vector_io provider integration itself.

**Correction 3 — Vector storage and application storage are independent configurations.** The OGX vector_io provider configuration (`remote::pgvector` via `ENABLE_PGVECTOR`) is completely separate from OGX's application storage backend configuration (`storage.kv.type`, `storage.sql.type`). This strategy only needs to configure the pgvector vector_io provider — it does not change the application storage backend, which remains on its existing default (SQLite). There is no SQLite-to-PostgreSQL migration concern because the application storage is not being touched. Remove any references to consolidating vector and application storage in a single database, and remove any SQLite-to-PostgreSQL upgrade path considerations.

# Operator-managed PostgreSQL/pgvector provisioning for Gen AI Studio playgrounds

## Description

Implement self-provisioning of the default PostgreSQL/pgvector instance in the
RHOAI-controlled operator layer for Gen AI Studio — the operator delivered by the
dashboard operator modularization (RHAISTRAT-7164) — following the pattern the
model-registry-operator uses for its auto-provisioned PostgreSQL. This epic exists only
if the go/no-go decision selects the operator path (the modularization lands in time for
the target release). The database runs as a separate process from the OGX instance and
is scoped per playground namespace.

## Scope

- Reconciler logic in the RHOAI-controlled Gen AI Studio operator that creates a
  PostgreSQL Deployment (pgvector-capable), Service, credentials Secret, and persistent
  storage in the playground's namespace when a playground with RAG is configured, using
  the existing Red Hat PostgreSQL image that already includes pgvector
  (`registry.redhat.io/rhel9/postgresql-16`) — no custom image build and no new pipeline
  onboarding.
- Lifecycle management via the reconciliation loop: the instance is created with the
  playground and removed when the playground is deleted; secret/credential handling
  follows the model-registry-operator pattern.
- Per-namespace isolation: the database is reachable only within its own namespace; no
  cross-namespace access.
- Resource requests/limits starting from the model-registry-operator's PostgreSQL
  reference sizing, adjusted per the sprint-1 benchmark recommendation.
- Disconnected-install support through the existing RELATED_IMAGE PostgreSQL image
  reference mechanism already present in the operator CSV.
- Expose the connection reference (credentials secret) for consumption by the playground
  OGX instance's pgvector vector_io provider configuration.

## Acceptance Criteria

- With a playground with RAG configured, the operator provisions a running PostgreSQL
  instance with the pgvector extension available in the playground's namespace —
  including credentials secret and persistent storage — without any user action.
- Deleting the playground removes its database instance and associated resources.
- The database is reachable only from within its own namespace (isolation verified from
  a second namespace).
- Resource requests/limits on the provisioned instance match the benchmark-informed
  recommendation derived from the model-registry-operator reference sizing.
- The PostgreSQL image reference is overridable for disconnected installs via the
  RELATED_IMAGE mechanism, verified by pointing it at an internal registry mirror.
- No custom container image is built or onboarded as part of this epic (the existing
  Red Hat PostgreSQL image with pgvector is reused).

## HLR Traceability

- Strategy acceptance criterion: a default vector store is available out-of-the-box
  without users manually provisioning or configuring external infrastructure.
- Strategy acceptance criterion: the default vector store runs as a separate process,
  decoupled from the OGX instance.
- Strategy acceptance criterion: the default vector store is scoped appropriately for
  multi-tenant environments (per-namespace isolation).
- Strategy acceptance criterion: the default vector store is lightweight enough for
  resource-constrained environments.
- Staff Engineer Input: self-provisioning follows the model-registry-operator pattern in
  the RHOAI-controlled operator; the Red Hat PostgreSQL image already includes pgvector;
  no Konflux onboarding needed; resource sizing references the model-registry-operator.

## Risks / Notes

- This epic exists only on the operator-path outcome of the go/no-go decision; the
  delivery timing of the dashboard operator modularization (RHAISTRAT-7164) is outside
  this strategy's control and gates whether this work can begin.
- The operator layer this epic extends is delivered by RHAISTRAT-7164; coordinate the
  provisioning reconciler design with that strategy's owners to avoid conflicting
  controller designs.

# End-to-end validation of Playground RAG with the operator-provisioned default vector store

## Description

Validate the complete out-of-the-box experience on the operator path: Gen AI Studio
playground RAG workflows function against the operator-managed default pgvector-backed
vector store with no loss of current capability and no manual setup steps, in
multi-tenant and resource-constrained conditions. This epic exists only on the
operator-path outcome of the go/no-go decision.

## Scope

- End-to-end test scenarios for playground RAG against the default store: document
  upload, embedding, indexing, retrieval, and grounded generation.
- Regression comparison against the current capability set: every playground RAG
  capability available with the inline provider passes with the default store.
- Multi-tenant verification: two playgrounds in different namespaces cannot access each
  other's vector data (per-namespace isolation).
- Resource-constrained environment verification: the playground and its default store
  operate within the benchmark-informed resource envelope on a constrained cluster.
- Disconnected-install validation of the full default-store path (image reference
  override plus playground RAG workflow).
- Performance sanity check against the captured inline Milvus baseline: ingestion and
  retrieval within the same order of magnitude (development-experimentation scope; no
  latency SLAs).
- A published validation report summarizing results and any remediation taken.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A freshly configured playground with RAG works end to end with zero manual database
  setup or configuration steps.
- The full existing playground RAG capability set passes the end-to-end suite against
  the default store with no functional regression.
- Per-namespace isolation is verified: cross-namespace access to another playground's
  vector data fails.
- The playground and its default store operate within the recommended resource envelope
  on a resource-constrained cluster.
- The disconnected-install scenario passes with the PostgreSQL image reference pointed
  at an internal registry mirror.
- Measured ingestion and retrieval performance is within the same order of magnitude as
  the captured inline Milvus baseline.
- The validation report is published and states pass/fail for each criterion above.

## HLR Traceability

- Strategy acceptance criterion: Gen AI Studio playground RAG workflows function with
  the default vector store with no loss of current capability.
- Strategy acceptance criterion: a default vector store is available out-of-the-box
  without manual provisioning or configuration.
- Strategy acceptance criterion: the default vector store is scoped appropriately for
  multi-tenant environments.
- Strategy acceptance criterion: the default vector store is lightweight enough for
  resource-constrained environments.
- Strategy success criterion: users experience no functional regression when inline
  providers are removed from the OGX distribution.
- Staff Engineer Input: validate pgvector only for Gen AI Studio Playground RAG
  workflows (Auto Rag compatibility is out of scope, deferred to RHAISTRAT-7824);
  benchmark criterion is order-of-magnitude, not a threshold.

## Risks / Notes

- Requires the pgvector provider wiring, the operator-managed provisioning, and the
  inline Milvus baseline to be in place before the comparison scenarios can run.

# BFF-managed PostgreSQL/pgvector provisioning for Gen AI Studio playgrounds

## Description

Implement provisioning of the default PostgreSQL/pgvector instance directly in the
gen-ai BFF, using the same pattern the BFF already applies when provisioning guardrails
infrastructure — for the outcome where the RHOAI-controlled operator layer from the
dashboard operator modularization (RHAISTRAT-7164) is not available in the target
release. When a playground with RAG is configured and no database instance exists in the
namespace, the BFF creates one; the database runs as a separate process from the OGX
instance and is scoped per playground namespace.

## Scope

- BFF logic that creates the PostgreSQL Deployment (pgvector-capable), Service,
  persistent volume claim, and credentials Secret in the playground's namespace when a
  playground with RAG is configured and no instance exists, using the existing Red Hat
  PostgreSQL image that already includes pgvector (`registry.redhat.io/rhel9/postgresql-16`)
  — no custom image build.
- Portability by design: the BFF consumes the database through a connection reference so
  that, when the platform-provided shared PostgreSQL becomes available via the DSC in the
  following release, it can consume the shared connection string instead of
  self-provisioning, without user-facing change.
- Lifecycle management design and implementation, giving explicit attention to the facts
  that the BFF is not an operator with a reconciliation loop: cleanup of database
  resources on playground deletion, handling of database pod restarts, and a credential
  rotation approach.
- Per-namespace isolation: the database is reachable only within its own namespace.
- Resource requests/limits starting from the model-registry-operator's PostgreSQL
  reference sizing, adjusted per the sprint-1 benchmark recommendation.
- Bring-your-own PostgreSQL fallback documentation: user-configured OGXServer connection
  details, in case BFF-managed lifecycle management proves unworkable during design.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Configuring a playground with RAG results in a running PostgreSQL instance with the
  pgvector extension available in the playground's namespace — including credentials
  secret and persistent storage — with no user action beyond normal playground setup.
- Deleting the playground cleans up the provisioned database resources.
- Documented and implemented behavior exists for database pod restarts and credential
  rotation (the BFF's non-operator lifecycle handling is explicitly designed, not
  incidental).
- The BFF consumes the database via a connection reference that can be swapped to a
  platform-provided shared database without changing user-facing behavior.
- The database is reachable only from within its own namespace (isolation verified from
  a second namespace).
- Resource requests/limits on the provisioned instance match the benchmark-informed
  recommendation derived from the model-registry-operator reference sizing.
- No custom container image is built as part of this epic.

## HLR Traceability

- Strategy acceptance criterion: a default vector store is available out-of-the-box
  without users manually provisioning or configuring external infrastructure.
- Strategy acceptance criterion: the default vector store runs as a separate process,
  decoupled from the OGX instance.
- Strategy acceptance criterion: the default vector store is scoped appropriately for
  multi-tenant environments (per-namespace isolation).
- Strategy acceptance criterion: the default vector store is lightweight enough for
  resource-constrained environments.
- Staff Engineer Input: BFF-managed provisioning is the alternative fallback if
  RHAISTRAT-7164 does not land in time, mirroring the guardrails provisioning pattern;
  portability to the 3.6 shared database and lifecycle management (cleanup, restarts,
  credential rotation) need explicit design attention; bring-your-own PostgreSQL is the
  further fallback.

## Risks / Notes

- This epic exists only on the BFF-managed outcome of the go/no-go decision.
- Lifecycle management is the design risk the Staff Engineer Input calls out: if the
  design exceeds a sprint of effort, split lifecycle management (restart/rotation
  handling) into a follow-up epic rather than expanding this one; if it proves
  unworkable altogether, fall back to bring-your-own PostgreSQL as documented in the
  scope.

# Configure the pgvector vector_io provider for Gen AI Studio playground OGX instances

## Description

Wire the pgvector remote vector store provider into the OGX instances the gen-ai BFF
creates for playgrounds with RAG, so vector storage is served by a separate
PostgreSQL-backed process instead of the inline provider bundled in the OGX distribution
image. Per the Staff Engineer Input, the existing remote vector store implementation is
largely reusable and the majority of the overall effort is database provisioning (handled
separately, per the selected provisioning approach); this epic covers the provider
configuration wiring only.

## Scope

- In the gen-ai BFF's OGXServer instance creation for playgrounds (the playground
  configuration path in the dashboard's gen-ai BFF), activate the pgvector vector_io
  provider (the remote `remote::pgvector` provider via its `ENABLE_PGVECTOR` environment
  guard) when RAG is configured for the playground.
- Point the provider at a PostgreSQL connection reference (credentials secret) supplied
  by whichever provisioning mechanism is selected — operator-provisioned, BFF-provisioned,
  or user-provided — so the wiring itself is approach-independent.
- Leave the OGX application storage configuration untouched (existing SQLite defaults
  for key-value and SQL storage). No vector/application storage consolidation and no
  SQLite-to-PostgreSQL migration: vector storage and application storage are independent
  configurations.
- Verify the OGX distribution's remote pgvector provider requires no distribution-side
  code change (the provider ships in the distribution); raise any gaps found with the
  OGX maintainers.
- Unit and integration tests for the provider configuration path, including the negative
  case (RAG disabled → provider not activated, no database reference required).

## Acceptance Criteria

- When the gen-ai BFF creates an OGXServer instance for a playground with RAG enabled,
  the created instance activates the pgvector vector_io provider backed by the referenced
  PostgreSQL connection, and vector storage is served by that separate database rather
  than an inline provider.
- When RAG is not enabled for a playground, the pgvector provider is not activated and
  no database reference is required.
- Application storage settings of created OGXServer instances remain on their existing
  defaults; no storage migration or consolidation is introduced.
- The connection reference is consumed generically: operator-provisioned,
  BFF-provisioned, and user-provided PostgreSQL instances all work without changes to
  this wiring.
- The provider configuration is reversible by configuration alone (switching to another
  remote vector provider requires no code change), preserving a rollback path while
  inline providers are being removed from the distribution.
- Tests covering the activated, deactivated, and connection-reference-consumption cases
  pass in the dashboard CI.

- Strategy acceptance criterion: the default vector store runs as a separate process,
  decoupled from the OGX instance (not an inline provider).
- Strategy acceptance criterion: Gen AI Studio playground RAG workflows function with
  the default vector store (this epic delivers the provider integration those workflows
  run against).
- Staff Engineer Input: vector_io provider configuration is independent of the OGX
  application storage backend; the existing remote vector store implementation is
  reusable; the effort focus is provisioning, not provider integration.

## Risks / Notes

  playground's usage, a distribution-side change may be needed after all — escalate
  immediately, as it would add an OGX work stream not currently in this decomposition.

The Staff Engineer Input section is non-empty and takes precedence over the AI-generated
strategy (whose full attachment was not available — see Health Warnings). Overrides applied:

1. **Auto Rag decoupled.** Auto Rag removed from affected components, acceptance criteria,
   and validation requirements; Auto Rag/pgvector compatibility is deferred to
   RHAISTRAT-7824 (targeting the next release). Only Gen AI Studio Playground RAG
   workflows are validated in this strategy.
2. **PostgreSQL is new work, not an extension.** OGX defaults to SQLite for application
   storage; the claim that every OGX instance already requires PostgreSQL is incorrect.
   Introducing PostgreSQL/pgvector is new provisioning work.
3. **No custom image build, no Konflux onboarding.** The existing Red Hat PostgreSQL
   image (`registry.redhat.io/rhel9/postgresql-16`) includes pgvector; the
   model-registry-operator already auto-provisions it, and the RELATED_IMAGE reference
   exists for disconnected installs. The 1-2 sprint image-onboarding estimate is eliminated.
4. **Vector storage is independent of application storage.** Only the vector_io provider
   (`remote::pgvector` via `ENABLE_PGVECTOR`) is configured; application storage stays on
   SQLite. All SQLite-to-PostgreSQL migration/consolidation concerns are removed.
5. **Performance thresholds removed.** The default store is for development
   experimentation; no latency SLAs. The sprint-1 benchmark verifies pgvector is in the
   same order of magnitude as the inline Milvus baseline; flat scan (no index) suffices.
6. **Provisioning approach is conditional on RHAISTRAT-7164.** Operator-pattern
   self-provisioning requires the RHOAI-controlled operator from the dashboard operator
   modularization (RHAISTRAT-7164, In Progress) — a hard dependency. If it does not land
   in time, fallbacks are BFF-managed provisioning (guardrails pattern) or bring-your-own
   PostgreSQL. A go/no-go gate is to be defined in sprint planning.
7. **Resource sizing** starts from the model-registry-operator's PostgreSQL
   requests/limits, adjusted by the sprint-1 benchmark.
8. **Platform-provided shared PostgreSQL via DSC** is the long-term direction but will
   not be available until the following release; any provisioning built here must be
   portable to it (consume a connection string rather than assume self-provisioning).
